NB2_INV1_SCOPE_CORRECTION.the_conflict_the_IC_named: v1.0.0's INV-1 read: 'No node of class HOSTED_MUTATION or EXTERNAL_AUTHORITY may begin before DN-1 has completed with a fresh measurement.' DN-15 and DN-17 are BOTH class EXTERNAL_AUTHORITY. DN-17's own asserted_non_edge in DAG_EDGES states explicitly: 'DN-17 (alert 1) does NOT depend on any node.' INV-1's prose and DAG_EDGES' own graph therefore directly contradicted each other for DN-17: the prose gated it behind DN-1, the graph declared it independent of everything.
NB2_INV1_SCOPE_CORRECTION.root_cause: INV-1 was written as a CLASS-LEVEL rule (every HOSTED_MUTATION or EXTERNAL_AUTHORITY node) when the actual justification for gating behind DN-1 is NODE-SPECIFIC: whether that particular node's correctness depends on the Vercel production-branch prestate. HOSTED_MUTATION and EXTERNAL_AUTHORITY are classes of ACT, not classes of DEPENDENCY, and conflating the two produced a rule broader than any edge in the graph could support.
NB2_INV1_SCOPE_CORRECTION.the_corrected_scope: INV-1 is CORRECTED to name the exact node set, computed as the transitive closure of DN-1's outgoing edges in DAG_EDGES (as amended below), rather than a node class: 'No node in {DN-7, DN-8, DN-9, DN-10, DN-11, DN-12, DN-14, DN-15} may begin before DN-1 has completed with a fresh measurement. This set is PROVABLY EQUAL to the set of nodes reachable from DN-1 by directed edges in DAG_EDGES (as amended), verified by explicit graph traversal rather than asserted by class membership. DN-16 (class NO_OP) and DN-17 (class EXTERNAL_AUTHORITY) are class members that are DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, because neither node's correctness depends on the Vercel production-branch prestate DN-1 measures - see the per-node justifications immediately below for the two nodes NEWLY added to the set, and the parent's own reasoning, unchanged, for why DN-17 was always independent.'
NB2_INV1_SCOPE_CORRECTION.why_DN-17_stays_excluded: DN-17 (secret-scanning alert 1 adjudication) operates entirely on GitHub's repository-level secret-scanning surface. Nothing DN-0 re-derives (the eight blob pins, the integration head/tree) and nothing DN-1 measures (the Vercel production-branch setting, its automatic-deployment toggle, its deploy-hook inventory) has any bearing on whether a credential was exposed or on PR #206's rotation/severity/disclosure/closure findings. v1.0.0's own asserted_non_edge for DN-17, and EAD-2's 'gated on NOTHING in this DAG,' are BOTH CORRECT and are left UNCHANGED. What was wrong was INV-1's class-level prose contradicting them, not the graph itself.

why_DN-14_is_newly_added.v1.0.0s_claim_being_superseded: DN-14's own 'independence_derived_here' field asserted: 'DN-14 does NOT depend on DN-1, DN-7, DN-8, DN-9, DN-10 or DN-11. Its only hard prerequisite besides freshness is its own prestate capture, plus the constraint that it precede DN-15.'
why_DN-14_is_newly_added.why_that_claim_does_not_survive_scrutiny: M-6's action (configuring an Ignored Build Step for integration/commercial-v1, narrowing automatic Previews) is treated by the parent's own Q_human_confirmation_points as requiring only REQUIRED, not ELEVATED, confirmation - a posture the parent reserves for mutations that 'can change what is publicly served.' That REQUIRED-not-ELEVATED classification is safe ONLY because integration/commercial-v1 is assumed NOT to be the production branch. If DN-1's fresh measurement ever finds the production branch is NOT main - in particular if some future hosted state has coupled it to integration/commercial-v1 - applying an Ignored Build Step to integration/commercial-v1 would SILENTLY STOP PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENTS, converting a low-risk Preview-narrowing act into an unannounced production outage. DN-14's low-severity confirmation posture is therefore CONDITIONED on knowing, freshly, that integration/commercial-v1 is not the production branch - which is precisely what DN-1 exists to establish rather than assume.

why_DN-15_is_newly_added.the_hazard: DN-15 creates an ACTUAL new deployment on integration/commercial-v1 under PR201's grant (not merely a configuration toggle, unlike DN-14). It runs AFTER DN-14 has already narrowed automatic Previews on that same branch specifically to prevent the ADJUDICATIONS.H hazard - an automatic Preview built with corrected configuration becoming indistinguishable from the governed one. If the production-branch assumption underlying DN-14's safety posture is wrong, the SAME confusion the M-6-before-PR201 ordering exists to prevent is live for DN-15's own deployment too, in a MORE severe form, because DN-15 creates a real deployment rather than suppressing one.
why_DN-15_is_newly_added.why_a_direct_edge_and_not_only_the_trans: DN-1 -> DN-14 -> DN-15 already implies DN-1 precedes DN-15 transitively. A DIRECT edge is added anyway, on the SAME precedent v1.0.0 itself set at DN-1 -> DN-9 (kept explicit despite being transitively implied by DN-1 -> DN-8 -> DN-9, 'stated explicitly rather than left transitive because DN-9 is the node most likely to be run first by a lane optimising for the integration line'). DN-15 is class EXTERNAL_AUTHORITY, governed by PR201's OWN authority; a lane executing PR201 in isolation is more likely to consult DN-15's own prerequisites list directly than to cross-reference DN-14's chain, exactly the same risk the DN-1->DN-9 precedent was recorded to guard against. EAD-1 already imposes an explicit prerequisite on DN-15 beyond its class defaults (PMV-2 for U-4); this is a second one, of the same kind.

NB3_DN0_EDGE_AND_CLASS_CORRECTION.the_conflict_the_IC_named: v1.0.0's DAG_EDGES.edges[0] read: 'DN-0 -> every other node.' Taken literally, this asserts an edge INTO DN-13, DN-16 and DN-17, each of whose DAG_NODES.prerequisites array is EMPTY ([]), and directly contradicts DN-17's own asserted_non_edge ('DN-17 does NOT depend on any node'). A wildcard edge that a node's own declared prerequisites, and a node's own asserted non-edge, simultaneously deny is not a consistent graph.
NB3_DN0_EDGE_AND_CLASS_CORRECTION.the_corrected_rule: The wildcard is REPLACED by a DEFERENCE rule, which by construction can never contradict a node's own prerequisites or an asserted non-edge, because it does not assert anything independently of them: 'DN-0 precedes every node N such that DN-0 appears in N.prerequisites, as DAG_NODES itself declares it - never asserted as an edge independent of that declaration. Concretely: DN-1 through DN-12, plus DN-14 and DN-15 (fourteen of the eighteen nodes, including the two DN-1 edges this amendment adds to DN-14 and DN-15's own prerequisites arrays under NB2 above) all name DN-0 in their own prerequisites. DN-13 (NOT_TRIGGERED), DN-16 (NO_OP) and DN-17 (EXTERNAL_AUTHORITY) each carry an EMPTY prerequisites array BY DESIGN and are correctly excluded: DN-13 and DN-16 perform NO act at all under the current owner set, so there is nothing for a freshness rebaseline to protect; DN-17 runs entirely on GitHub's secret-scanning surface, untouched by anything DN-0 re-derives (the eight blob pins, the integration head and tree, the acting worktree's own branch and HEAD).'
NB3_DN0_EDGE_AND_CLASS_CORRECTION.why_this_is_the_correct_fix_and_not_mere: A narrower wildcard (e.g. 'DN-0 -> every node except DN-13/16/17') would still be an INDEPENDENT assertion that could drift out of sync with DAG_NODES.prerequisites the next time a node's prerequisites are edited, exactly the failure mode that produced this defect. The deference rule cannot drift: it is DEFINED as reading DAG_NODES.prerequisites, so it is definitionally always in agreement with it. This is a self-consistency fix, not merely a corrected enumeration.

the_node_class_enumeration_defect.finding: DAG_NODES.rule enumerates five classes: READ_ONLY_MEASUREMENT, OWNER_DECISION, HOSTED_MUTATION, NO_OP, EXTERNAL_AUTHORITY. DN-13's own 'class' field is the literal string 'NOT_TRIGGERED' - a SIXTH value, used in a node but never declared in the rule that is supposed to enumerate every class a node may carry.
the_node_class_enumeration_defect.corrected_enumeration: NOT_TRIGGERED is ADDED as a sixth class, defined: 'NOT_TRIGGERED is derived when a ratified owner selection does NOT call for the act at all under the CURRENT owner set, as distinct from NO_OP (the owner selected an outcome IDENTICAL to the current state - see NO_OP_NODES.NON-1 vs NON-2 for the full worked distinction v1.0.0 already draws in prose, now backed by a declared class). A NOT_TRIGGERED node carries no live authority obligation under the current owner set but is NOT retired: it re-enters under its OWN existing authority, as its own named class (typically HOSTED_MUTATION), the instant a future owner decision calls for it, with none of its original prestate, confirmation or rollback requirements weakened by the interval spent NOT_TRIGGERED.' This closes the gap between the prose v1.0.0 already wrote (NO_OP_NODES.NON-2, which correctly explains the NOT_TRIGGERED/NO_OP distinction) and the class enumeration that never named it as a class at all.

NB3_DN0_EDGE_AND_CLASS_CORRECTION.verification_this_amendment_performed: Confirmed programmatically: with the DN-0 deference rule applied to the fourteen nodes whose own prerequisites array names DN-0, and DN-13/DN-16/DN-17 left at their declared empty prerequisites, the resulting edge set is IDENTICAL to what P4 (structural acyclicity/closure) already checks against DAG_NODES.prerequisites - meaning the deference rule and the node-level prerequisites arrays, once DN-14 and DN-15 are corrected per NB2, are now PROVABLY the same relation stated twice, which is the property a wildcard cannot have and a deference rule always does.
